audit_scope: Independent arithmetic, density integrals, physical bounds, feature provenance and declared validation. Passing verifies reproduction and mathematical implementation, not physical truth, predictive universality, or independent-discovery status.

limits: Whole-galaxy transfer is exploratory reuse, not an independent survey.
Mass proxy uses common stellarM/L and stellar light radius; no full baryonic geometry or nuisance likelihood.
Affine halo-state laws do not reproduce full abundance-matching/CDM priors or unify every scale.

cosmological_halo.independent_method: Immutable photometric-input identity; independent density integral and critical-density radius construction; all forecasts, structural states, diagnostics, fits, minima, exclusions, comparator copies and bootstraps. No analysis-code imports.
limits: Mref is dark-matter-only-equivalent reference M200c; dark component is (1-fb)Mref. This is an explicit deterministic convention, not an empirical halo mass measurement.
Mass mapping and concentration are conditional on common photometric stellar M/L and an approximate HI-plus-stellar mass proxy.
Published concentration-mass calibration is extrapolated for some low-mass objects; scatter and baryonic halo response are omitted.
Fixed Planck cosmology and concentration-mass relation supply structural priors, not a full LambdaCDM prediction.
No observed radius tests the imposed outer truncation; finite total mass is a declared extrapolation.
The three-coefficient size-model RMS advantage is small, changes sign across CV seeds and has descriptive intervals spanning zero; median speed error is worse than RAR.
No per-galaxy target-informed halo parameter is fitted in held-out forecasts; affine mapping coefficients are shared.

gas_bridge.independent_method: Raw component and source joins; adaptive integration of cluster gas density and mass-profile derivatives; all forecasts, fits, objective minima, metrics, exclusions, paired host resampling and nonpositive-force retention. No analysis-code imports.
limits: One eta is used across gas phases, but disk constant-weight source scaling and spherical finite-Rc cluster integral are different geometry calculations.
A disk evaluation radius cutoff cannot bound finite-Rc source approximation error: exterior sources contribute. No exact finite-Rc disk reconstruction is present.
The cold-HI versus hot-ICM extension is the tested hypothesis; the published hot-gas-only model is not falsified by its failure.
Cluster zero values in disk-only ggas/gstar columns are unused placeholders; measured cluster gas enters through nonzero source-density quadrature.
Disk-only fits do not identify Rc; cold-to-cluster transfer assumes external fixed Rc=400 kpc.
Frozen CLASH coefficients include CLASH targets from earlier work, so CLASH scores are descriptive. All newly refitted test targets are excluded as declared.
Cluster speed percentages are algebraic square-root transforms, not measured disk orbital-speed errors.
Resampling intervals are descriptive conditional on frozen forecasts and omit calibration/systematic/model-selection uncertainty.

field_bridge.independent_method: Exact rationalized translated Plummer sphere; independent infinite-support scalar integrals; source joins, all predictions, objectives, minima, metrics and complete galaxy/host exclusions. No analysis-code imports.
limits: General 1+2alpha bound is necessary only for isolated spherical finite nonnegative baryon source at its baryon half-mass radius.
Sharper 1+alpha bound needs a radially nonincreasing source density such as Plummer.
Dwarf accelerations use a half-light estimator and assumed stellar mass-to-light ratios; binaries, anisotropy, tides and host field are not modeled.
Finite satellite host density and external-field contributions are absent: this does not exclude every formulation of NLG or MOG.
Stationary kernels provide no fitted time history or evidence for discrete spacetime.
mu saturates the fitted bound and the short-range limit is effectively a common multiplicative mass enhancement, not a resolved finite length measurement.
